items.title: id(world): actor-authorized builder install + moderator revoke (design #835 phase 2)
items.body: Phase 2 of the design in `doc/2026-11-01_design_id835.md` for #5544 (phase 1 journal gate merged as PR #4535). - `WorldCommand::RevokeAuthorized` / `InstallProgramAuthorized` take the live `JoinCapability`; the serialized world actor authorizes it (`MODERATOR` / `BUILDER`) at the mutation boundary and derives the audit actor for `Revoked { by }` / `BuilderInstalled { by }`. No caller-supplied actor ID is trusted on this path. - Revoke keeps fail-closed in-memory semantics but surfaces a journal-append failure instead of reporting an audited success. - Install runs through the existing admin install path with `installed_by` set, preserving the atomic `Committed` + `BuilderInstalled` transaction. - `authorize()` fix: `effective_scopes` seeds from `WorldScopes::ALL`, which deliberately excludes the admin authority bits, so `authorize(token, BUILDER|MODERATOR)` could never succeed. `authorize` now seeds the ancestor-chain intersection with all recognized bits (the intersection only removes bits; ceilings, delegation and projections keep the `ALL`-seeded path). Tests: `pkgs/id/tests/world_roles.rs` gains moderator-revoke/guest-denial, builder-install/guest-denial, and revoked-moderator-denial cases with journal-attribution assertions (oracle: the journal entries recorded by a capturing journal). Full `id` package suite verified on the laptop. Phase 3 (joined-session frames, `actor_denied` wire code, Wasm-only builder installs) remains and is tracked as a follow-up on #5544. items.title: feat(pm-stack): remediation executor — caps, cooldowns, circuit breakers, deploy lock (#9989)
items.body: Implements the remediation executor (design note §2, #1260 follow-on 2). Pure decision/state module in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/remediation.ts`: - §2 catalogue of stateless actions only (Pad/Grist/databases deliberately excluded — never auto-restarted). - Per-action attempt caps + cooldowns; per-facet daily cap (6) and global daily cap (15). - Per-facet circuit breaker opens after 3 exhausted incidents in 24h, stays open 24h. - Deploy-lock precondition: refused and journaled. - One action in flight at a time. - Stateful facets (pad/grist/database) refused as `stateful`. - Journal entry returned on every decision (allowed or refused). - Serializable state for durable persistence by the host. Tests: `pm-stack/aggregator/test/remediation.test.ts` — 24 cases covering caps, cooldowns, breakers, deploy lock, daily caps, stateful refusal, serialization. Closes #9989. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.body: ## What this adds The design note for **#6004** (wave-2 follow-up of the worlds programme #5955, parent topic #5973): what authority id should reserve to the server/world admin **from day one**, and what is genuinely delegable to a world community — argued from LambdaMOO's documented 1990–1996 governance arc (wizards → 1992 devolution → 1993 ballot system → Mr. Bungle → 1996 recentralization). New record: `doc/2026-11-08T12-50-00Z_design_id6004_lambdamoo_governance_arc/`, linked from `doc/README.md`. ## Contents - **§1 Reserved authority** — a table of what cannot be outvoted, each row tied to the surface that already exists in `pkgs/id` (BUILDER install path, capability ceilings, admin token, resource envelope, MODERATOR revoke, host serving policy), with the two invariants that follow: no governance body may widen its own authority, and every exercise of reserved authority is a logged entry referencing what it changed. - **§2 Delegable to the community** — content rules and parameters, reviewer sets, appeals, pre-approval of in-world submissions, moderation-pack adoption/parameterization, and quota policy within the envelope. Includes the Mr. Bungle lesson mapped to id's actual surface: attribution is reserved (per-user function mapping #5967), delegation is always a strict subset (DELEGATE/attenuation), presentation may change how a participant looks but never who they are or what they did, and a moderation library never acts *as* a participant. - **§3 Quota as a governance tool** — LambdaMOO's base allocation plus discretionarily granted increases judged on quality/utility, read as the missing per-principal building quota in id; grants are logged content decisions, never envelope changes, and never a punishment lever. - **§4 The reserved-authority checklist** — 18 numbered items in three groups (world admin / host operator / delegable) plus the three platform invariants nobody delegates. ## Scope Docs only, no code. The note supplies the authority split #5973's own deliverable must respect; it does not design the moderation-library interface, the pre-approval binding, or the quota data model (each named as a remaining decision in §5). Closes #6004. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR?
